title: Hugo's Wobbly Tower
markdown:
Whoooo! Gather ‘round, little sprouts. An old owl’s tale, carried on the breeze, whispers of Hugo’s toy shop, a cozy nook filled with sunshine and happy days.

Now, consider this: Hugo wanted to build a tall tower. He stacked round balls next to blocky cars, and put a fuzzy bear right on top. Whoosh! A gentle breeze came in. The tower wobbled and tumbled! The toys rolled and clattered everywhere.

Bloom the bee buzzed in. "Oh dear!" she hummed. Miss Maple, the wise tree outside, rustled her leaves. "Patience now," she whispered. "Every tumble teaches."

Hugo looked at the jumbled toys. How could he build it so it wouldn't fall? Bloom zipped around. She nudged a round ball. It rolled away! She nudged a blocky car. It wiggled but stayed put. "Hugo!" she buzzed. "The round ones roll, and the flat ones stay still!"

Hugo picked up a ball. It felt ready to roll. He pushed it. It slid like a tiny explorer. He picked up a blocky car. It slid too, but stayed more grounded. "You're right, Bloom!" Hugo beamed. "Round toys roll, flat toys stay steady!"

Miss Maple’s leaves rustled. "Indeed," she whispered. "Flat sides are like steady feet. Round sides are like cheerful wheels."

So, Hugo built his tower again. This time, he placed the round toys inside sturdy boxes, like treasures. He stacked the steady, flat toys high, their sides fitting together like puzzle pieces. His new tower was grand and tall, reaching for the sunbeams.

"Whooo could have guessed?" Hugo chuckled. "It’s their shapes! Round ones roll, flat ones stay put!" Bloom buzzed a happy tune. Hugo smiled, a quiet wonder blooming inside him. He looked at the toys, little teachers, and wondered what other shape secrets the world held.
characters: Hugo the toy fixer, Bloom the bee, Miss Maple
